title: Law evidence record (BRIEF P6, §6, §7 — Grade S, owned by tannen)
description: One record per law run, emitted by the laws runner and stored content-addressed (the record's id is the content address of its canonical encoding and is therefore not a field of the record). Frozen at m0-laws-freeze; vectors under tests/laws/evidence-vectors/. This is the future belief-update stream for the Governor seam.

law_id.description: The law identifier as named in the milestone spec (e.g. L0.4).

law_nodes.description: How many of the law's test functions reported a result. A record is written only when every one the frozen law file defines did (BRIEF §5.11), so at a given descriptor this is the law's whole node count.

test_cases.description: How many test INVOCATIONS reported a result: parametrised cases counted one apiece, so this exceeds law_nodes exactly where a law is parametrised. NOT a count of generated examples — one @given invocation is one test case here however many examples it drew.

examined.description: What the run actually EXAMINED (D0117), beside the verdict of whether it passed. Optional: absent is read as 'this runner did not measure', so records written before this field existed keep their meaning, and absent stays distinct from a run that examined nothing. Present, it must be whole — a half-given measure is one a reader has to guess about.

run_at.description: Wall-clock timestamp of the RUNNER (effectful shell), never of the kernel; RFC 3339.

seed.description: The generator seed/derandomisation token for property laws; null for example-only laws. Recorded so every verdict is replayable (BRIEF P6).

descriptors.description: Descriptor refs the run covered (empty for laws over the encoding alone). Refs use the pinned grammar (concepts/provenance-ref-grammar.yaml).

packages.description: Version-relevant packages (at minimum pytest and hypothesis).
